title: RESOLVED: the 3/16 constant is now verified against the primary source
expected: Control 6 requires both that the scan be directly cited AND that the attributed 3/16 statement be supported
observed: The citation is now present in all six artifacts, including both rendered PDFs, and a search index confirms the URL designates the right paper. But http://ordman.net/MathResearch/CEOClique_Parts.pdf returns HTTP 302 to the https form, whose certificate is expired (SEC_E_CERT_EXPIRED). The auditor declined to disable certificate validation. The scan could not be read.
impact: CLOSED. The owner supplied the scan (downloaded from the cited URL in their own browser after the auditor's four retrieval routes all failed). The auditor rendered and read it: Theorem 1, page 23, reads 'For all split graphs G_n, cp(G_n) <= (3/16) n^2 + O(n)', and the abstract on page 21 states the same constant. Attribution SUPPORTED with pinpoint. Disclosed as owner-supplied evidence verified by the auditor, not an independent retrieval.
reproduction: curl the http URL and observe the 302; attempt the https URL and observe the expired certificate
proposed_disposition: No further action; the constant is verified. See RES-V13-004 for the remaining accessibility issue.

title: The cited author-hosted URL is unusable as printed because the host serves an expired certificate
expected: A reader following reference [2] should be able to retrieve the scan
observed: ordman.net issues HTTP 302 from http to https, and the https certificate is expired (SEC_E_CERT_EXPIRED). Four auditor retrieval routes failed: WebFetch https, curl http, the internal browser, and a web.archive.org snapshot. The owner could retrieve it only by clicking through the browser certificate warning.
impact: The 3/16 constant is now VERIFIED (Theorem 1, page 23), so this is no longer an evidentiary gap. What remains is that the printed citation does not resolve cleanly for a reader. Cosmetic/accessibility only. The defect is on a third-party host and cannot be fixed by editing the target.
reproduction: Attempt the printed https URL and observe the expired certificate; attempt the http form and observe the 302
proposed_disposition: Optionally note in the manuscript that the host currently serves an expired certificate, or cite a stable mirror or DOI alongside it
